[bold][color=#ffffff]Info[/color][/bold]
Space Law is a tool used to benefit the sector, not a cudgel. The greater good of the station is to be considered during sentencing. Space Law is designed to protect the station and crew, not to hinder them. Station-wide emergencies are to take priority over enforcing Space Law. Roleplay fun is to take priority over all others.
Read [textlink="RP-First Sentencing" link="SOPSecurityOverviewRPFirstSentencing"] in Security Overview before applying charges. Space Law is meant to support roleplay, reward cooperation, and avoid punitive maximization.
## RP-First Sentencing
[bold]The purpose of Space Law is to create better roleplay, not to "win" against another player.[/bold] Officers, Wardens, and Command are expected to apply the law in ways that preserve scenes, reward cooperation, and let people lose gracefully when doing so does not meaningfully endanger the station.
[bold]Maximum punishment is not the default.[/bold] If several lawful outcomes are available, prefer the one that creates the best scene, the clearest consequence, and the most room for continued play. A suspect who is cooperative, entertaining, remorseful, or trying to turn a scene into good roleplay should usually receive more discretion than one who is hostile, evasive, or repeatedly destructive.
Security should actively look for RP-forward alternatives when they fit the facts, including:
- Reducing to a lesser included offense when the circumstances reasonably support it. - Applying [textlink="M13 — Cooperation with Security" link="HLSpaceLawList"] generously when a suspect plays along, turns themselves in, or helps move the scene forward. - Offering work duty, cleanup, restitution, or community service in place of, or in partial substitution for, straight brig time when the offense and station conditions allow. - Letting a suspect argue for a lower charge or lighter sentence in-character when they make a coherent case. - Preserving harmless or low-impact gimmick items when keeping them clearly improves the scene and does not create a meaningful security risk.
Examples of good "losing gracefully" and RP-first enforcement:
- If a suspect makes a convoluted but entertaining in-character legal argument, it is acceptable to let that argument partially work when the result is still plausible under Space Law. - If pirates or similar raiders return and one wants to keep a pet coconut, toy, or other low-stakes gimmick item, security may allow it when the player gives a good in-character reason and the item is not meaningfully dangerous. - Do not search a PDA, bag, headset, or other item for contraband based on out-of-character suspicion or antag meta knowledge. Searches and escalations must be based on in-character facts, lawful cause, and observable behavior. - If a prisoner is cooperative and clearly engaging with the scene, offer alternatives to the harshest available outcome: reduced time, work duty, restitution, or a negotiated charge reduction. - If a crew member is "playing nice," officers should use that to build scene value rather than shutting it down with every possible stacked penalty, search, and enhancement.
This discretion is not permission to ignore serious threats. It is permission to remember that the goal is station roleplay first, legal procedure second, and punitive maximization last.
### Sentencing Reference
The following table defines the baseline sentencing range for each crime tier, to provide context when applying [bold]M02 — Elevated Sentencing[/bold] (which elevates a charge by one tier).
Tier
Typical Sentence
[bold]Infraction[/bold]
Fine only: 10–25k speso; no brig unless fine is evaded
[bold]Minor Crime[/bold]
Up to 10 min brig; fine optional
[bold]Misdemeanor[/bold]
5–15 min brig; 20–45k speso fine
[bold]Felony[/bold]
10–20 min brig; 35–85k speso fine; possible demotion
[bold]Capital Crime[/bold]
Permanent Confinement, Execution, or Force Borgification
### Lesser Included Offenses (No Stacking)
When two charges describe the same criminal act at different severities, only the greatest applicable charge should be applied.
[bold]Stacking is not permitted.[/bold] Security may not charge both a greater offense and its lesser included offense for the same underlying act. The greatest offense should be charged, but may be reduced to a lesser included offense at officer discretion.
[bold]Trespass and Breaking and Entering are legally distinct offenses.[/bold] [textlink="109/209/309" link="HLSpaceLawList"] govern unlawful presence in a restricted area; [textlink="110/210/310" link="HLSpaceLawList"] govern the act of forcible entry. When both the unlawful entry and the unlawful presence are established, both charges may apply.
